changes: Demand and supply both stepped up: data center revenue $107.6bn (+21% QoQ); Rubin nearly $20bn of revenue, 'our fastest architecture ramp ever'; supply commitments $390bn (from $279bn).
Guarantees rose to $118.0bn from $108.5bn; a new $9.5bn 'power and systems credit support' line appeared next to the $105bn SB Energy Ohio support for OpenAI and $3.5bn for neoclouds.
Neocloud commitments ('AI cloud agreements', renamed) fell to $32bn from $36bn and are now stated as conditional on the neocloud securing financing and Nvidia accepting the deployed capacity.
Data center leases not yet commenced reached $74bn (cloud service agreements plus leases $102bn, from $74bn); equity commitments fell to $20bn from $25bn.

Kress, as interim CEO, said future support will focus on land, power and shell and be 'disciplined and selective', with investment-grade customers 'very helpful'; the chairman said Huang will not be reinstated and the CEO search will not be rushed.

Independent fact-check by a fresh agent with sources only: about 95 items confirmed against the release, CFO commentary, 2Q 10-Q and transcripts; 13 corrections applied (off-balance-sheet sum restated to $272bn; unsupported pricing, memory, staff and 'standalone CPU' wording removed; DSO 45-day history dropped; call vs commentary attributions fixed). Opex and trend labels are judgments; Microsoft pull-back is from Bloomberg (5 Nov) via the preview.
consensus_thesis: Investors own Nvidia for supply-constrained AI demand and 74-75% gross margins, but going in they were pricing leadership risk after Jensen Huang's resignation and growing vendor-financing exposure (about $108.5bn of guarantees at 2Q); the stock closed at $155.46 on 17 November, about 35% below the ~$239 record close of 6 October cited in the preview.
headline: The demand case strengthened and needs no change; the vendor-financing exposure grew again, but it is now more explicitly conditional, so credit quality holds rather than weakens.
kona: Nvidia said future support will go to land, power and shell, 'disciplined and selective', with investment-grade customers seen as helpful, and that its guarantees only attach once a building is ready for service. That makes Kona's category the one Nvidia prefers to support, but its support cannot de-risk construction: Kona still needs its own construction finance, with Nvidia support, if any, refinancing it at energization. With neocloud commitments now conditional on the neocloud raising money, Kona should not treat a GPU-owner tenant's Nvidia agreement as credit support and should prefer hyperscaler-backed or prepaid tenants. It should also check whether the new Commerce Department export controls change GPU shipments to Argentina.

sections.body: Emphasized more: conditionality of guarantees and neocloud commitments; land, power and shell as the preferred form of support; supply-chain deals (Kinsus, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, SPIL); the $2.5T cloud backlog figure. Less or dropped: Huang's '100%' growth framing (Moore raised it; Kress did not address it); the 'AI cloud agreements' label; no new frontier-lab investment figure. KPIs more important: guarantees by type, leases not commenced, DSO, neocloud commitments. Less: China revenue (now excluded from guidance). Risks up: guarantee exposure, lease commitments, receivables, export rules. Down: margin floor (called the bottom), leadership disruption to near-term execution.

rows: Guarantees rose $9.5bn to $118.0bn with a new 'power and systems credit support' line. Who is the counterparty, what triggers it, and is there a board-set cap on total credit support?

Neocloud commitments fell to $32bn from $36bn. Was any commitment cancelled because a neocloud failed to raise financing, and which partners account for the drop?
Credit and demand: early sign of neocloud funding stress.
DSO rose to 64 days from 60. What share of the $81bn of receivables is on extended terms, and are any neocloud receivables past due?
Credit: customer stress shows here first.
FY28 growth was raised to about 75%, conditional on 'customers' access to capital'. How much of FY28 revenue is from customers whose financing Nvidia supports?
Equity: how much growth is self-financed.
